title: Four Operations and Number Sense
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Four Operations and Number Sense. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

coverage: Fractions, decimals and checking inverse operations

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Four operations and place value

Add and subtract by aligning place-value columns. Multiplication distributes over addition: (\(a(b+c)=ab+ac\)). Division asks how many equal groups or how many units fit; for integers, (\(a=bq+r\)) with (\(0 \le r0\)).

Signed numbers

Adding a negative is subtraction. Subtracting a negative is addition. For multiplication and division, equal signs give a positive result and different signs give a negative result. Division by zero is undefined.

Fractions and decimals

Add fractions using a common denominator. Multiply numerators and denominators; for division, multiply by the reciprocal of a nonzero divisor. Convert terminating decimals to fractions by place value when useful.

Worked example: Evaluate (\(18-2 \times (3+4)\)). First the bracket gives 7, then multiplication gives 14, and subtraction gives 4. Estimate and reverse operations to check arithmetic.

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• Estimate the size and sign of the answer before calculating exactly.
  • Align decimal points for addition and subtraction; preserve place value when multiplying.
  • For division, check using (\(dividend=divisor \times quotient+remainder\)).
  • Reduce fractions before multiplying to keep numbers small.
  • Follow operation precedence and use parentheses to remove ambiguity.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• Commutative: addition and multiplication; subtraction and division are not commutative.
  • Associative: addition and multiplication; grouping matters for subtraction and division.
  • Distributive law: (\(a(b+c)=ab+ac\)).
  • For nonzero a, (\(a/a=1\)); zero has no reciprocal.

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    Evaluate (\(8+6\cdot2\)).

    1. (\(20\))
    2. (\(28\))
    3. (\(32\))
    4. (\(14\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(20\))

    Multiply first: (\(6\cdot2=12\)). Then (\(8+12=20\)).

  2. Core:

    Evaluate (\(45\div5+7\)).

    1. (\(9\))
    2. (\(12\))
    3. (\(16\))
    4. (\(52\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(16\))

    Divide first: (\(45\div5=9\)); then (\(9+7=16\)).

  3. Foundation:

    Evaluate (\(-8\))+13.

    1. (\(-21\))
    2. (\(-5\))
    3. (\(5\))
    4. (\(21\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(5\))

    Starting at -8 and moving 13 units right gives 5.

  4. Standard:

    Calculate (\(3/4 \div 2/5\)).

    1. (\(3/10\))
    2. (\(5/6\))
    3. (\(15/8\))
    4. (\(8/15\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(15/8\))

    Divide by a fraction by multiplying by its reciprocal: (\(3/4 \times 5/2=15/8\)).

  5. Challenge:

    When 157 is divided by 12, what are the quotient and remainder?

    1. (\(q=12,r=13\))
    2. (\(q=13,r=1\))
    3. (\(q=13,r=13\))
    4. (\(q=14,r=-11\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(q=13,r=1\))

    (\(12 \times 13+1=157\)), and the remainder 1 satisfies (\(0 \le 1<12\)).
